headline: US suspends Microsoft and Adobe from green card path over alleged fraud
summary: The U.S. government has blocked Microsoft, Adobe, and several IT outsourcing firms from the PERM program, a key step for H-1B workers seeking green cards, citing alleged fraud and abuse.
details: The U.S. administration has halted all new and pending Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) applications for Microsoft, Adobe, and major IT outsourcing firms including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy, Wipro, HCL, and Capgemini. This action prevents H-1B visa holders at these companies from progressing towards U.S. green cards.

Vice President JD Vance stated that Microsoft, in particular, has "abused this system more" than any other company. He alleged that for every worker Microsoft laid off, the company hired one and a half foreign workers on H-1B visas, citing 6,000 layoffs against 6,300 H-1B approvals and nearly 3,000 green card applications.

Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling explained that Microsoft and Adobe's PERM privileges were revoked due to "multiple active federal investigations." The government claims these companies have engaged in fraud and abuse within the H-1B and PERM programs.

This crackdown follows a broader investigation launched by the Labor Department into alleged fraud and human trafficking within the H-1B and PERM programs. Concerns include fraudulent applications, wage manipulation, coercion, and 'benching,' where H-1B employees are kept on payroll without active work.

The move aligns with a tighter grip on the H-1B program, including an executive order signed by President Trump in September aimed at curbing abuse. Recent changes to H-1B lottery rules reportedly prioritize highly skilled and highly paid workers.
caption:
Microsoft and Adobe are suspended from the U.S. green card program for H-1B workers over alleged fraud.

The U.S. administration has halted all new and pending Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) applications for Microsoft, Adobe, and major IT outsourcing firms including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy, Wipro, HCL, and Capgemini. This action prevents H-1B visa holders at these companies from progressing towards U.S. green cards.

Vice President JD Vance stated that Microsoft, in particular, has "abused this system more" than any other company. He alleged that for every worker Microsoft laid off, the company hired one and a half foreign workers on H-1B visas, citing 6,000 layoffs against 6,300 H-1B approvals and nearly 3,000 green card applications.

Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling explained that Microsoft and Adobe's PERM privileges were revoked due to "multiple active federal investigations." The government claims these companies have engaged in fraud and abuse within the H-1B and PERM programs.

This crackdown follows a broader investigation launched by the Labor Department into alleged fraud and human trafficking within the H-1B and PERM programs. Concerns include fraudulent applications, wage manipulation, coercion, and 'benching,' where H-1B employees are kept on payroll without active work.

The move aligns with a tighter grip on the H-1B program, including an executive order signed by President Trump in September aimed at curbing abuse. Recent changes to H-1B lottery rules reportedly prioritize highly skilled and highly paid workers.
